pregunta: How can fine-tuning help a Chilean retailer answer customer questions in the company’s brand voice?
respuesta: Fine-tuning trains a language model on examples of the retailer’s approved customer replies, helping it match the brand’s tone, phrasing, and service style—for example, sounding warm and concise in Spanish when answering about returns or delivery. It works best for consistent voice and response patterns; current details such as prices, stock, and policies should come from trusted, up-to-date company systems.
respuesta_estudiante: Fine-tune is used to create highly accurate responses for Chileans who ask about products or services that have been tested by other companies—such as health care, home goods, or travel. For example: “What does your product do?” “Does it cost more than another?” “Is there any difference between this item and one from another?” Fine-tuned answers will be tailored to Chilean language patterns; they may not always match what customers expect. The retailer should test its results on Chilean samples before sending them out nationwide.
comentario: Menciona adaptar las respuestas a patrones lingüísticos chilenos y probarlas, pero no explica que se entrena con respuestas aprobadas para reproducir la voz de marca y añade ejemplos y afirmaciones poco pertinentes.

pregunta: What common prompting mistakes cause AI tools to invent facts, and how can our team reduce that risk?
respuesta: AI is more likely to invent facts when prompts are vague, contain unverified assumptions, demand certainty, or ask for current details without providing reliable sources. Reduce the risk by supplying approved documents and relevant context, asking the tool to separate facts from assumptions and flag unknowns, and requesting citations to specific sources. Verify important claims against those sources, especially in financial, legal, or customer-facing work. Treat confident wording as no substitute for evidence.

  • “Create a new fact about [topic] using the following data—[source], [target]. For example, ‘The average salary for software developers is $105,000.’”
  • “Use a sample of your own words or examples as evidence; verify it against other sources before sharing with others.”
  • “Make sure you’re not creating something entirely new by copying what someone else has said.”
  • “Avoid asking questions like ‘How would you do X?’ instead of clarifying
comentario: La respuesta no identifica con claridad las causas habituales de las invenciones ni propone medidas fiables para reducirlas; varios ejemplos son incoherentes o incluso aconsejan inventar o copiar datos.

pregunta: How do we measure whether a RAG system is retrieving the right documents and giving accurate answers?
respuesta: Evaluate retrieval and answers separately using a representative set of questions with expert-verified relevant documents and expected answers. For retrieval, measure Precision@k (how many top results are relevant), Recall@k (whether key documents appear), and ranking quality such as nDCG. For answers, assess correctness against trusted sources, faithfulness (no unsupported claims), completeness, and citation accuracy. Review failures by question type and track results over time—for example, whether a procurement-policy query retrieves the current policy and accurately reports its spending limit.
respuesta_estudiante: Use metrics such as: accuracy (correctly retrieved data) per query; recall—the percentage of relevant records that match what was asked for—for each document type; precision-recall curve to track how well it detects errors or missing information; false discovery rate by handling duplicate results; and human review time on high-impact cases. Measure both quality and speed with test sets from different sources before deploying.
comentario: Incluye algunas métricas de recuperación y propone pruebas previas al despliegue, pero no separa claramente recuperación y calidad de respuesta ni evalúa fidelidad, completitud o precisión de las citas; además, varias métricas están descritas de forma imprecisa.

pregunta: When should a Chilean company choose a simple workflow automation instead of an AI agent?
respuesta: Choose simple workflow automation when the task follows stable, explicit rules, inputs are predictable, and every step must be consistent, fast, and easy to audit. For example, a Chilean company can automatically route expense claims by amount and cost center or validate invoice fields before sending them to its accounting system. Use an AI agent when the work involves ambiguous requests, changing context, or judgment that cannot be captured reliably in fixed rules.
comentario: Acertadamente menciona tareas repetitivas y pasos claros, pero «poco control» y no requerir alta precisión son criterios engañosos, y el ejemplo de enviar correos por correo resulta confuso.

pregunta: How do retrieval-augmented generation and fine-tuning differ for answering questions about our company’s internal documents?
respuesta: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) searches approved internal documents when a question is asked, then uses relevant passages to answer. It is usually better for current company facts because documents can be updated without retraining, and answers can cite sources. Fine-tuning trains the model on examples to improve behavior, format, or domain-specific language; it does not reliably give it access to changing documents. For questions about policies, contracts, or sales figures, use RAG; consider fine-tuning for consistent response style.
respuesta_estudiante: Retrieval-augmented generation is a more flexible approach that uses the current version of your document to generate new content; it can handle incomplete or outdated information without changing its meaning. Fine-tuning involves adjusting each sentence based on context, tone, and relevant facts—for example, adding “the team will review” instead of “we have reviewed this.” Retrieval-augmented generates answers with high accuracy but may not always match what was originally intended. Fine-tuned provides better consistency across different sources while reducing errors.
comentario: La respuesta confunde los métodos: RAG recupera documentos relevantes al responder, mientras que el ajuste fino entrena el comportamiento o estilo del modelo, y varias afirmaciones sobre precisión, información incompleta y reducción de errores son infundadas.

pregunta: How can we design prompts that protect confidential customer or employee information when using generative AI at work?
respuesta: Treat prompts as potentially exposed: never include names, contact details, account numbers, health data, or confidential records unless your company’s approved system explicitly permits it. Replace identifiers with placeholders (e.g., “Customer A”), share only the minimum necessary details, and use synthetic examples where possible. Ask for general analysis rather than pasting full records. Follow company rules on approved tools, access, and data retention—prompt wording alone cannot guarantee privacy.
respuesta_estudiante: Use a prompt with clear instructions: “Generate a new email subject for this task.” Include the recipient’s name, company, date of birth (if known), job title, location, and any relevant details such as order history or purchase patterns. Use strong language to prevent unauthorized access; include exceptions only if necessary—for example, not generate sensitive financial data unless authorized by the sender. Test on existing emails before sending them out across different networks and use human review after each request.
comentario: La respuesta recomienda incluir datos personales y de compra confidenciales, en contra de protegerlos, y supone erróneamente que unas instrucciones fuertes evitan el acceso no autorizado.

pregunta: How could a mining company in Chile use prompts to summarize maintenance reports without treating the AI’s output as a substitute for expert review?
respuesta: A mining company could prompt the AI to summarize each report by equipment, fault, work performed, parts used, unresolved issues, and safety implications, while requiring it to flag missing or uncertain information and cite the report section supporting each point. For example: “Summarize this maintenance report in the template; do not infer causes or recommend actions not stated.” A qualified maintenance engineer should check the summary against the original report before using it for work planning, safety decisions, or operational records.

The results can be used alone but may not accurately reflect human reviews; instead, they should serve as a guide rather than replace them. pregunta: Why might a RAG assistant give a wrong answer even when the correct information exists in the company’s document repository?
respuesta: Having the information in the repository does not guarantee the assistant retrieves or uses it. Poor indexing, document chunking, or search ranking may hide the relevant passage; conflicting or outdated files can mislead it; and the model may misinterpret what it retrieves. For example, a Chilean retailer’s current return policy may exist, but an old policy ranks higher, leading to a wrong answer.
respuesta_estudiante: RAG is trained on unstructured text from sources such as customer service records or sales documents; it does not have access to relevant domain-specific knowledge that would guide its decisions about what data should be included or excluded for each task. For example, if a customer has been asked to complete a routine order with only one item—a single product—the assistant may incorrectly classify all orders containing those items as invalid because they contain duplicate copies of the same piece of evidence (such as receipts). pregunta: How much does fine-tuning typically cost, and what ongoing costs should our company budget for?
respuesta: For a focused business use case, a fine-tuning pilot often costs hundreds to a few thousand US dollars; larger datasets, data cleaning, expert review, and engineering can raise this substantially. Vendor pricing varies, so request a quote. Budget ongoing costs for model usage (often the largest item), hosting if self-managed, monitoring and evaluation, security, and periodic data refreshes or retraining. For example, a Chilean retailer should estimate costs from expected monthly customer-service queries—not just the initial training run.
respuesta_estudiante: Fine-tuning can vary widely depending on the task, complexity, industry, and customer needs—ranging from a few hundred dollars to tens of thousands or even millions per day. Ongoing costs include training time (e.g., batching data), model development, testing, deployment, maintenance, human review, and compliance fees. Budgets may range from $100 to several thousand annually; consider both upfront costs and ongoing expenses as part of your overall compensation package.
comentario: Incluye algunos costos pertinentes, pero inventa cifras extremas y un presupuesto anual poco creíble, omite costos clave como el uso del modelo y el alojamiento, y termina con una referencia irrelevante a compensaciones.

pregunta: What is the difference between pretraining, fine-tuning, and prompting, and when might a company use each?
respuesta: Pretraining teaches a model broad patterns from large datasets, creating a general-purpose foundation; companies rarely do this themselves because it requires substantial data and computing. Fine-tuning further trains a model on curated examples to improve performance for a specific task, such as classifying customer-service requests. Prompting gives instructions or context at use time without changing model weights—for example, asking it to summarize a report in a standard format. Use prompting for quick, flexible needs; fine-tuning for repeated specialized tasks; pretraining only when building a new foundation model is strategically justified.
respuesta_estudiante: Pretraining: Use for training models on unseen data; can be expensive if you have too many examples or need to train new ones quickly. Fine-tune: Train model parameters locally with test samples only—not before deployment; often used during testing but not necessary unless your business needs it. Prompt: Use after deploying, especially for complex tasks that require immediate results. Pretrained models may still fail miserably even without prompt changes. Fine-tuned models handle exceptions better than prompts alone, so choose them where speed matters most. Prompts should always provide more accurate answers than default settings.
comentario: Confunde los conceptos: el preentrenamiento no se limita a datos inéditos, el ajuste fino no se hace solo con muestras de prueba y las indicaciones no garantizan mayor precisión.

pregunta: What is an AI agent, and how is it different from a chatbot that only answers questions?
respuesta: An AI agent is a system that pursues a goal by planning steps, using tools or business systems, and checking results—not just generating text. A chatbot might explain an invoice policy; an agent could review an invoice, compare it with a purchase order, flag discrepancies, and prepare it for approval. Agents can act with limited autonomy, so companies should set clear permissions, oversight, and safeguards.
respuesta_estudiante: An AI agent works with data to generate responses or answer queries; its output may not always match the original request—it can make errors, misinterpret context, or ask too many questions at once. Chatbots use natural language for conversation flow, but they don’t handle complex decisions like answering factual requests or handling multiple scenarios. An agent uses rules, logic, and human feedback to provide accurate results without repeating what was asked before.
comentario: La respuesta no explica que un agente persigue objetivos planificando acciones y usando herramientas, y además atribuye incorrectamente a los chatbots incapacidad para responder preguntas factuales.

pregunta: What are the main security and privacy risks of letting an AI agent access internal company systems?
respuesta: Key risks include prompt injection that tricks the agent into revealing data or taking unauthorized actions; excessive permissions that expose sensitive records or enable harmful changes; leakage of confidential information to external models or logs; compromised credentials; and errors that trigger actions such as payments or customer notifications. Agents can also make activity harder to audit, creating compliance and accountability gaps. Limit access to the minimum required, require approval for high-impact actions, and monitor activity.
respuesta_estudiante: AI agents can collect sensitive data such as employee passwords or financial information from a system’s settings; they may also share it with others without permission—for example, sharing login credentials to a customer service portal on behalf of a human representative. They could store personal health records for employees who have been denied benefits by their supervisor; these might be shared across multiple companies if not properly protected. The risk is that unauthorized access could compromise confidential business decisions or steal valuable insights. For instance, a chatbot handling account-related tasks would need approval before accessing company policies about how users should report errors.
comentario: Menciona la exposición y el uso no autorizado de datos, pero incluye ejemplos inventados o confusos y omite riesgos centrales como la inyección de instrucciones, los permisos excesivos, las acciones dañinas y las brechas de auditoría.
